questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code manages sockets? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A relay accepts the TCP connection but never replies. What happens?
choices: The probe hangs until the OS TCP keepalive gives up
The socket is closed by the peer, so the probe resolves via the 'close' handler
After timeoutMs the timer calls finish, which destroys the socket and resolves with healthy: false
The promise rejects with a timeout error that sweep must catch

questions.prompt: After finish() calls socket.destroy(), the 'close' event fires. What effect does it have?
choices: None: settled is already true, so the second finish call returns immediately
It resolves the promise a second time with 'closed before reply'
It overwrites the healthy result with an unhealthy one in the registry
It throws because the socket is already destroyed

questions.prompt: With 200 relays and maxConcurrentProbes = 10, how many sockets can be open at once during a sweep?
choices: 200, because Promise.all starts all probes immediately
At most 10, because 10 workers each await one probe before taking the next endpoint
At most 1, because the workers share the next counter
It is unbounded if overlapping sweeps start from setInterval
